heading: REGENT OF BOYOLALI,

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definitions

heading: Article 1
translated_text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Boyolali Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent...................
3-

4. Regent is the Regent of Boyolali.

Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is

5. a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administrator.

Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in

6. administering governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region. Regional Technical Implementation Unit is a technical implementation unit formed by
7. the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, who need special protection, and other problems.

Integrated Service Center is a non-structural institution that

8. coordinates the implementation of an integrated service system for women victims.

Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and

9. existence of humans as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.

Women's Empowerment is all efforts to improve

10. physical, mental spiritual, social abilities, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.

Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at

11. protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.

Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that

12. directly or indirectly is based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of Human Rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.

Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and

13. responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women

14. to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
15. Violence....................
4-

15. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differentiation that results in, or could result in physical, psychological and/or sexual suffering to women, including threats, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of private life.
16. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of Human Rights caused by gender-based role labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life.
17. Disaster is an event or series of events that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of the community caused by natural factors and/or non-natural factors as well as human factors resulting in human casualties, environmental damage, property losses, and psychological impacts.
18. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
19. Elderly is a person who has reached the age of 60 (sixty) years and above.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
21. Persons with Disabilities are persons who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
22. Manpower is every person who is able to perform work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for the Community.
23. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
24. Data and Information System is the collection, management, and utilization of Women's data needed in the Implementation of Women's Protection and Empowerment.

Elderly Women

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

1. Implementation of protection for elderly women in order to extend life expectancy so they can carry out their social functions and play an active role naturally in their social life.
2. Elderly women as referred to in paragraph (1) receive the right to Protection over:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal assistance, mobility, social services, public facilities, and buildings; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. Implementation of protection for women with disabilities in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) receive the right to protection over:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal assistance, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 11

1. Implementation of protection for domestic women workers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relations.
2. Women................
(2) Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection over:
a. recognition of rights, wages, and decent working conditions;
b. health insurance and employment social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and
d. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

heading: Part Seven

Women as Family Economic Pillars

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

1. Implementation of protection for women as family economic pillars in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women as family economic pillars.
2. Women as family economic pillars as referred to in paragraph (1) receive the right to protection over:
a. acts of discrimination and efforts to weaken the function of women as family economic pillars;
b. strengthening capacity and recognition as family economic pillars in their environment; and
c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.

Article 13

2. Women former residents of correctional institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection over:
a. social rehabilitation and social reintegration; and
b. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Political and Governmental Field

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

Women's Empowerment in the political and governmental field includes:

(1)

a. involvement of women in decision-making in the field of development and life at various levels;
b. provision of opportunities for women to hold public office;
c. participation in general elections; and
d. self-development through organizations to associate, assemble, and express opinions.

(2) Women's Empowerment in the political and governmental field as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(3) The Regional Government provides guarantees to women to have the right to vote and/or be elected in general elections, regional head elections, village head elections and/or other political office elections based on equal rights through direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair voting according to the provisions of laws and regulations.

(4) The Regional Government provides opportunities for women to be appointed as Regional Government officials and occupy strategic positions in Regional Government.

5. The Regional Government and/or political parties may provide political education for women.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Legal Field

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. Women's Empowerment in the legal field includes:
a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the legal field through communication, information, and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
2. Women's Empowerment in the legal field as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Education Field

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. Women's Empowerment in the education field through the provision of formal and non-formal education for women in the Region.
2. Women's Empowerment in the education field as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to improve women's capabilities.
3. Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) includes Women's Empowerment education, skills education, and job training.
4. Women's Empowerment in the education field is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Part Seven
translated_text:
Part Seven

Health Field

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

1. Women have the right to receive health services in order to undergo reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.
2. Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. health services before pregnancy, during pregnancy, childbirth, and after childbirth;
b. regulation of pregnancy, contraceptive services, and sexual health; and
c. reproductive health services.
3. Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented through promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative approaches.

heading: Part Eight
translated_text:
Part Eight

Employment Field

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. Women have equal opportunities without Discrimination to obtain employment.
2. Employers who employ female Workers must provide protection that includes welfare, safety, and health.

heading: Part Nine
translated_text:
Part Nine

Social Security Field

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

1. The Regional Government is responsible for providing guidance facilities for women with social problems.
2. The Regional Government provides rights to social security for women with social problems.
3. The responsibility for providing guidance facilities for women with social problems is under the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 25

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the protection and Empowerment of Women.
2. The protection and Empowerment of Women efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs, and activities.
3. Efforts...................
15- (3) The protection and Empowerment of Women efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

STRATEGY FOR PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

Article 26

1. The Protection and Empowerment of Women shall be implemented by integrating Gender mainstreaming and Gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. The Protection and Empowerment of Women shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

MECHANISM FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND

EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

Article 27

The mechanism for the implementation of Protection and Empowerment of Women shall be carried out through the following stages:

a. formulation of policy planning for programs and activities;
b. budgeting of programs and activities;
c. implementation of programs and activities; and

d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities as referred to in Article 27 letter a, shall be implemented consisting of:
a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data;
b. coordination and synchronization of the preparation of planning for programs and activities with related Regional Apparatus; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
3. Formulation................
16- (3) The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities for the implementation of protection and Empowerment of Women shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning.

4. The budgeting of programs and activities as referred to in Article 27 letter b, shall be implemented through general budget policies set forth in the Regional revenue and expenditure budget.
5. The implementation of programs and activities as referred to in Article 27 letter c, shall be implemented consisting of:
a. implementation of programs and activities set forth in the budget documents of the Regional Apparatus work unit;
b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of activity programs with the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and child protection.
6. The implementation of monitoring, evaluation, and reporting as referred to in Article 27 letter d, shall be implemented consisting of:
a. conducting monitoring and evaluation periodically on the implementation of programs and activities that have been carried out;
b. preparing reports periodically; and
c. evaluation results as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the following year.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 29

1. In the context of implementing the protection and Empowerment of Women, the Regional Government shall establish:
a. Integrated Service Center; and
b. Regional Technical Implementation Unit.
2. In the implementation of services for women victims, the Regional Government shall establish an Integrated Service Center as a victim service network. (3) The establishment of the Integrated Service Center as referred to in paragraph (2) is so that women victims obtain comprehensive, integrated, quality, inclusive and sustainable services.

{4) At the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, a Regional Technical Implementation Unit shall be established to carry out technical operational activities and/or certain supporting technical activities for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

5. Provisions.................
17- (5) Further provisions regarding the Integrated Service Center and Regional Technical Implementation Unit shall be regulated by Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. In addition to establishing the Integrated Service Center and Regional Technical Implementation Unit as referred to in Article 29, the Regional Government may establish a task force and/or Regional action committee for Women's Protection.
2. The task force and/or Regional action committee for Women's Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be established to support the implementation of protection for Women from acts of violence.

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

1. The task force and/or Regional action committee as referred to in Article 30 is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating Women's Protection, prevention and handling of trafficking in persons.
2. Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties, and functions of the task force and/or Regional action committee as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

Part One

Coordination

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

In the context of implementing the protection and Empowerment of Women, the Regional Government shall carry out coordination with the central government, provincial government, other regency/city governments, related agencies, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, educational institutions, religious institutions, community social institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business world and other related stakeholders.

Cooperation

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. In the context of implementing the protection and empowerment of women, the Regional Government may conduct cooperation.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

DEVELOPMENT OF DATA AND INFORMATION SYSTEM

Article 34

1. The Regional Government shall establish an integrated and interconnected Data and Information System for the protection and Empowerment of Women.
2. The Data and Information System as referred to in paragraph (1) shall involve the government, provincial government and vertical agencies as well as stakeholders.
3. Data and information on the protection and Empowerment of Women shall be published to the Community and submitted to Regional Apparatus and related agencies for the development of programs and policies for Women's Protection.
4. The development of the Data and Information System for the protection and Empowerment of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and child protection and the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of communication and informatics.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 35

1. The Community may participate in the implementation of the protection and Empowerment of Women.
2. Participation.............
19- (2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be realized by:
a. actions to provide information and/or report Violence Against Women to law enforcement or the competent authorities, or participate in handling acts of Violence Against Women; and/or
b. provision of communication, information, and education media regarding empowerment and prevention of Violence Against Women within the Family, Community, educational institutions, and public spaces.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

FUNDING

Article 36

Funding, implementation of policies, and activity programs for the protection and Empowerment of Women shall be sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other legitimate and non-binding sources of funds.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 37

1. The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of the protection and Empowerment of Women.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 38
Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

1. Supervision as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) shall be in the form of monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of the protection and Empowerment of Women in the Region.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out with the principles of professionalism, transparency, and accountability.
3. The Community may conduct supervision of the implementation of the protection and Empowerment of Women organized in the Region.
4. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be carried out through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regional Government and/or the DPRD.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIV

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 40

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation must be stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 41.
translated_text:
Article 41.

Article 41

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Boyolali Regency.

heading: ELUCIDATION
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BOYOLALI REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

The State through the government and Regional Government according to their respective authorities is responsible for respecting, protecting, and guaranteeing the human rights of every citizen including women and children without discrimination, because women and children are part of Indonesian citizens who have the same rights as others, and the rights of women and children are human rights that must be guaranteed, protected not only by the government but also by the Regional Government.

Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation is expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.

Various forms of acts of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection for women.

Furthermore, in order to realize Regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation is a concrete manifestation of the Boyolali Regency Government in providing protection and ensuring the fulfillment of the human rights of Women in accordance with its duties and responsibilities.

Article 2

Letter a What is meant by "the principle of respect for Human Rights" is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women's rights as part of Human Rights.

Letter b What is meant by "the principle of justice and Gender Equality" is that in organizing the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and equality between men and women.

Letter c What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is that in the protection and empowerment of women it is carried out without regard to differences in both the regional dimension (disaster areas, conflict areas, border areas, disadvantaged areas, remote areas, and others), age dimension (productive age, elderly, and others), and special dimension (persons with disabilities, workers, and others).

Letter d What is meant by "the principle of victim protection" is that the protection and empowerment of women carried out by the Regional Government, business entities or the community is oriented towards the protection of women as victims.
